title: RadCalc — nuclide reference sheets and spectrum-solved shielding for radiation protection
description:
Reference sheets for 147 nuclides: half-life, decay mode, specific activity, photon, beta and alpha emission lines with each line's share of the air kerma rate, and — for photon emitters — half- and tenth-value layers solved across the whole emission spectrum rather than read from a single-energy table.

The spectrum solution matters where the dose rate is not dominated by one line. For Na-22 the lead half-value layer is 6.5 mm against the 10.5 mm implied by its strongest line at 1275 keV, which carries only 55% of the kerma. For Sn-113 the tenth-value layer is 84 times the half-value layer rather than the 3.32 that holds for a single energy, so stacking half-value layers does not work. All figures are narrow beam with no buildup.

Decay data are derived from the IAEA Nuclear Data Section Livechart (ENSDF) and used with acknowledgement under the IAEA terms of use; the IAEA does not endorse this work. Photon interaction coefficients are NIST Standard Reference Database 126 (Hubbell and Seltzer, NISTIR 5632, doi:10.18434/T4D01F), which is copyright the U.S. Secretary of Commerce with all rights reserved; those tables are NOT redistributed here — the harvest script is included so they can be obtained from NIST directly. NIST does not endorse this work.
